name: ARMORED CORE™ VI FIRES OF RUBICON™

Optimal.Notes: A 40 Hz refresh rate with a matching frame cap produces smooth, tear-free gameplay that feels noticeably better than 30 fps for this fast-paced action game. FSR upscaling from 1024x640 recovers sharpness while keeping GPU load manageable.

profiles.Summary: Armored Core VI is a demanding FromSoftware action game that runs on the Steam Deck at a playable level, though it requires lowered settings and upscaling to maintain stable frame rates. The game is rated Playable (not Verified) on Deck, and ProtonDB gold-tier reports suggest it works well under Proton with some tweaking needed for smooth performance.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck tuning guides were found; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum requirements (GTX 1650 minimum, which closely matches the Deck GPU) and the ProtonDB gold tier rating. On your first run, check frame pacing in a large open arena and during a boss fight — if the Optimal profile stutters, drop to Max Battery settings.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at sub-native resolution with Deck FSR keeps the GPU well within budget; the 8 W TDP and 900 MHz GPU clock prevent thermal throttling and maximize session length. Boss fights with heavy particle effects may briefly dip below 30 fps.

KnownIssues: Partial controller support only — some menus may require touchscreen or mouse input
Performance can dip noticeably in large open arenas and during heavy particle-effect boss fights
No native Linux build; runs via Proton, which may introduce occasional compatibility quirks
Text and UI elements can be small at native 1280x800 on the Deck screen

MaxPerformance.Notes: 60 fps is achievable in simpler environments but expect frequent dips to the mid-40s during intense boss encounters and particle-heavy combat; consider dropping the cap to 40 if stuttering is distracting. Battery life will be short at full TDP.

Optimal.Notes: 40 Hz mode with a locked 40 fps cap gives perfectly smooth, tear-free gameplay that suits the fast action well; medium textures keep mechs looking sharp without overwhelming the shared VRAM. Option names are estimated from typical FromSoftware/PC port settings — verify exact names in-game.
